title: Policy Regret and Honest Value Intervals under Weak Instrumental Quantile Regression
banked_reason: D0.5 clean rerun: mathematically sound, but subfield tier below field floor (paper score ceiling 6.9 < 7.4), not salvageable in scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered contribution is a matched weak-strength regret order and matching honest expected-diameter order, both attained by explicit lambda-blind residual procedures, but the frontier is only up to constants and is confined to a highly structured balanced-instrument, rank-invariant, additive positive-compliance model.

The Gaussian-plus-exponential experiment is proved only sequencewise in finitely many oracle-normalized coordinates, while whole-graph approximation, feasible saddle transfer, and simultaneous strength-section optimality remain open and therefore add no class-wide optimality result.

There is no stale framing claim about those open saddle problems, but the absence of an applied or numerical demonstration and the source-unverified comparison with the closest closed-form binary-IVQR literature limit the leading-journal case.
proof_attempt_summary: Five D0 solver rounds and a guarded rerun produced an exact observable reconstruction, a lambda-blind residual-moment policy attaining the matched weak-strength regret order, and an explicit uniformly honest optimal-value interval with matching expected-diameter order. The fixed-sequence Gaussian plus shifted-exponential limit and finite-state minimax convergence were derived, but the full estimated-fiber saddle, whole-graph approximation, and common strength-section minimizer remain open. The clean D0.5 review passed the mathematics and graded the delivered contribution subfield, below the field floor.
tldr: The statistical headlines are matched class-wide frontiers: \(R_n^*(\lambda)\asymp\min\{D,(\lambda\vee\eta_n)^{-1}\}\), attained by the named observed-data rule \(\widehat d_n^{\mathrm{res}}\) without \(\lambda\) or \(\kappa_n\) as input, and a uniformly honest interval for \(V_n^*\) whose worst-case expected diameter has the same sharp order. The underlying shared-rank IVQR geometry is reconstructed exactly from the pooled law \(\mu_n\) and label contrast \(T_n\). Along each fixed local sequence, oracle-normalized interior coordinates converge to \(X_0,X_1,X_\kappa\), moving-support extremes converge to independent shifted exponentials, and raw median gaps are stable under expanded-extreme support estimation. For every supplied finite oracle-normalized feasible state set, likelihood and minimax convergence and an exact Gaussian finite-game saddle are proved. Whole-graph risk-metric approximation, graph-specific finite-support geometry, a common minimizer across strength sections, and uniform attainment by the estimated spline saddle remain unresolved; the globally ridge-studentized multiplier interval is likewise not validated.
gap: Generic weak-GMM decision theory neither identifies the feasible state space created by shared ranks nor resolves the nonvanishing uncertainty in a local first stage. A support-normalized tangent written against the raw law is ill-typed, and a rule indexed by the unknown limit \(\lambda\) is infeasible.
fill: The common normalized chart, raw-scale pullback, and singular endpoint coordinates define one coherent experiment. A \(\lambda\)-augmented feasible-state net uses only observed empirical channels and yields a uniform adaptive transfer theorem over the compact strength range.
